correctness.rationale: Definition 5.1 quantifies truth preservation over every modal formula and tuple of names. In a classical language closed under negation, inclusion of complete truth sets is equality: if \(v\models\varphi\) while \(w\not\models\varphi\), then \(w\models\neg\varphi\), and preservation along \(wRv\) contradicts the truth of \(\varphi\) at \(v\). Thus the relation is symmetric; reflexivity and transitivity are immediate, so every resulting frame is an equivalence frame. The explicit reflexive nontransitive three-world constant-domain model with an unconstrained predicate satisfies the allowed base theory while falsifying an axiom-4 instance, so the advertised general completeness theorem cannot hold for the minimal reflexive modal extension. The bundled finite checker corroborates both elementary semantic facts but is not needed for the proof.
